validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #72 collects six follow-ups from the review and QA of PR #69 (for #42). The critique is empty — plan/critique.json is {} — so there was nothing to judge, and I re-derived every finding against the tree myself rather than accepting the proposal's report. All six still hold, and I reproduced four of them by execution.

TWO ARE REAL CODE DEFECTS.

(1) The forecast double-projects a posted-and-split schedule occurrence. packages/loot-core/src/server/forecast/app.ts:149 passes `transactions` — the result of getTransactions, which carries .options({ splits: 'inline' }) (forecast-filters.ts:83) — as buildFutureScheduleOccurrences's fifth argument, and that is the array indexed by indexPostedScheduleTransactions to decide isScheduleOccurrencePosted. I confirmed the mechanism in packages/loot-core/src/server/aql/schema/executors.ts:238-244: any split type other than 'all' appends is_parent = 0, so the inline set cannot see split parents. And the split parent is the ONLY row carrying the occurrence stamp — splitTransaction (shared/transactions.ts:404-408) keeps schedule/schedule_occurrence on the row it turns into a parent while makeChild (:57) copies neither onto children. So a posted-and-split occurrence is invisible to its own posted-check and gets projected a second time. The correct reader already exists: getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery (shared/schedules.ts:251) passes splits:'all' and returns exactly the three-column shape indexPostedScheduleTransactions is typed on. The forecast was the fourth reader and the only one on the default split type. Display-only — it cannot double-pay, since that is the guard #69 fixed.

(2) Unsplitting a posted schedule payment destroys it. makeAsNonChildTransactions (shared/transactions.ts:439) decides deleteParentTransaction from remainingChildTransactions.length <= 1 alone — a CHILD COUNT — rather than from whether the children's amounts account for the parent. A split opened from the register starts as two 0.00 children, so the count says 'safe' while the amounts say the parent is the only row holding any value, and the occurrence stamp with it. I called the function directly on a 12345 stamped parent with two 0.00 children: updated=[{amount:0},{amount:0}], deleted=[{amount:12345,schedule:'s1'}] — the payment and its stamp gone. The single-child branch at :452 already implements the correct behaviour; the general branch does not extend it.

TWO ARE DEFECTS IN #69's OWN TEST FILE. (3) The case 'leaves the status queries agreeing with the guard after a split' passes with the guard reverted. I removed .options({ splits: 'all' }) from schedules/app.ts and got exactly 1 failed | 51 passed, the failure being its sibling 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split'. Its name and comment claim a direction it does not test. The guard direction IS covered by the sibling, so this is a framing gap, not missing coverage. (4) readSplitFamily's raw SQL against v_transactions_internal rests on a comment that is false. I replaced its body with the AQL form the review proposed and the suite passed 52/52 — but only after two convention changes the proposal's own earlier draft missed (below).

TWO ARE PROCESS. (5) #69's title lacks the mandatory [AI] prefix. (6) #69's work order omitted its own release note from files[]. This order lists both notes.

plan/brief.md records no decisions and no 'Acceptance (from the split)' section, so the issue text plus the repo's own PR rules are the only constraints, and no IAC-n needs tracing. The brief's one prior rejection — AC-7/AC-8 being browser-verifiable criteria that nothing in the product can decide — has been honoured: both are gone from acceptance[] and live in qa_script and out_of_scope instead.
validated_work_order.root_cause:
Two independent defects sharing one shape: a consumer reads the (schedule, schedule_occurrence) stamp, or a transaction's amount, off a row set the default query shape cannot see.

The forecast reads the stamp off getTransactions' result, which passes splits:'inline' and therefore excludes split parents — the only rows carrying the stamp, since splitTransaction keeps schedule/schedule_occurrence on the row it makes a parent and makeChild copies neither onto the children. The correct reader already exists and is already used three times: getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery passes splits:'all' and returns exactly the ['schedule','date','schedule_occurrence'] shape indexPostedScheduleTransactions already expects. The forecast was the fourth reader and the only one on the default split type.

Unsplit: makeAsNonChildTransactions decides to delete the parent from the CHILD COUNT rather than from whether the children's amounts account for the parent. A register-made split has two 0.00 children, so the count says 'safe to delete' while the amounts say the parent is the only row carrying any value — and the occurrence stamp with it. The single-child branch at :452 already implements the correct behaviour; the general branch just does not extend it.
validated_work_order.approach:
Four code/test changes plus two release notes. Every prototype below was applied to this tree, measured, and reverted; the working tree is clean and only plan/ is untracked.

A. FORECAST (finding 1). Stop deriving the forecast's occurrence state from getTransactions. In forecast/app.ts import aqlQuery and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery, and after schedules is filtered fetch the posted-schedule-transactions query and pass its result as the fifth argument to buildFutureScheduleOccurrences in place of transactions. transactions still goes to projectForecastData untouched and MUST stay on the inline split set: there the CHILDREN carry the amounts the projection sums, which is exactly why the stamp cannot be read off it — widening it would double-count every split, and the existing test 'does not double-count split parents in posted transaction balances' is that guard. Retype buildFutureScheduleOccurrences's postedTransactions parameter from TransactionEntity[] to PostedScheduleTransaction[] and import the type (I hit this myself — the retype without the import does not compile). The parameter reaches only indexPostedScheduleTransactions, so the wide typing was looser than the use. I applied both edits: the forecast suite passed 22/22 and yarn typecheck was green across all six workspaces.

The retype is DOCUMENTATION, not a guard, and the order says so. TransactionEntity is structurally assignable to PostedScheduleTransaction (all three fields are optional-compatible and date is present), so passing the inline set back would still typecheck. The tests are what pin the behaviour, not the compiler.

B. UNSPLIT (finding 2). In makeAsNonChildTransactions, sum the children's amounts before the promote-and-delete result and narrow the parent's deletion from the child count alone to the amounts: when at most one child would remain (the existing deleteParentTransaction condition) AND that total does not equal the parent's amount, return the parent as the sole surviving row through the existing makeTransactionWithChildCategory helper — which preserves schedule and schedule_occurrence — with the children as deleted. When the children do sum to the parent, the existing path is untouched. Add a comment naming the invariant: a parent may only be deleted when the children account for it.

This must go through makeTransactionWithChildCategory, NOT merely by flipping the deleteParentTransaction boolean. I tried the cheaper version first: narrowing only the boolean leaves the row with is_parent: true and a spread of the parent, which is a worse outcome than today's — the amount survives but the row stays a split parent. The helper is what sets is_parent: false and takes the category from the promoted child.

I applied the fix and exercised it over six shapes, each matching the proposal's claims: unfilled 2-child unsplit-all now returns the 12345 stamped parent with is_parent: false and both children deleted; FILLED 5000/7345 still splits out into two rows with the parent deleted; partial 5000/0 keeps the parent at 12345; filled 3-child unselecting one leaves the parent at 8345 with the promoted child alongside; 3-child unselecting two keeps the parent at 12345; zero-amount parent with zero children unchanged. Full loot-core suite with both fixes applied: 87 files, 1268 passed, 1 expected fail, 2 skipped, exit 0.

C. TEST FRAMING (finding 3). Rename 'leaves the status queries agreeing with the guard after a split' to what it asserts — that the status queries still report a split-parented occurrence as posted — and replace its comment's guard-pinning claim with a pointer to the sibling that does pin it. No assertion changes.

D. TEST IDIOM (finding 4). Replace readSplitFamily's body with the AQL query, keeping the id/parent_id $or and selecting is_parent, parent_id, schedule, schedule_occurrence. The inline type literal, the internal view name and the 'read through AQL rather than off the raw view above' integer-date detour all go away. Delete the raw-SQL justification comment rather than rewriting it — its stated reason is false.

Two assertion-convention changes are REQUIRED alongside it, not optional: is_parent comes back as a boolean rather than 1, and schedule/schedule_occurrence come back undefined where the raw view returned null. Without changing expect(splitParent).toMatchObject({ is_parent: 1, ... }) to is_parent: true and the two child assertions to toBeFalsy(), the rewrite FAILS the suite on 'expected undefined to be null'. I confirmed both: it fails without them and passes 52/52 with them.

E. RELEASE NOTES. Two notes, not one. The forecast correction folds into the existing schedule-occurrence note, which shares its root cause and symptom. The unsplit fix gets its own note (fix-unsplit-empty-split.md): it is NOT schedule-specific — unsplitting any split that was never filled in destroys the row's amount, in any account, schedule or not — so folding it into a note about schedule occurrences would misdescribe it.

I did not split the ticket. The two defects are two views of one interaction — what happens to a schedule payment once it has been split — and the unsplit fix is the wider-reaching while the forecast fix is a one-line argument change, so 'do the small one first' does not apply either. Reasoning in alternatives_considered.

files.change: Import aqlQuery from '#server/aql' and, from '#shared/schedules', getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery and the PostedScheduleTransaction type. After schedules is filtered, add `const { data: postedScheduleTransactions } = await aqlQuery(getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery(schedules))` and pass it as the fifth argument to buildFutureScheduleOccurrences in place of transactions. transactions continues to projectForecastData unchanged and must stay on the inline split set — there the children carry the amounts the projection sums.
files.why: Fix for finding 1. getTransactions' inline split set cannot see a split parent, the only row carrying the occurrence stamp, so a posted-and-split occurrence is invisible to isScheduleOccurrencePosted and gets projected a second time. getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery already passes splits:'all' and returns exactly the three-column shape indexPostedScheduleTransactions expects.

files.change: Retype buildFutureScheduleOccurrences' postedTransactions parameter from TransactionEntity[] to PostedScheduleTransaction[] and ADD the `import type { PostedScheduleTransaction } from '#shared/schedules';` — without the import the file does not compile (I hit this applying the prototype). Drop TransactionEntity from the type import only if it becomes unused. No logic change. Comment the parameter to say the narrow type documents the three-column projection and is NOT a guard: TransactionEntity is structurally assignable to PostedScheduleTransaction, so passing the inline set back would still typecheck.
files.why: The parameter now receives a three-column projection rather than whole transaction rows, and the wide typing was looser than the use. The comment exists because the narrow type looks like it prevents the bug's return and does not — the tests are what pin it.

files.change: In makeAsNonChildTransactions, before the promote-and-delete result is computed, sum the children's amounts (newNonChildTransactions.map(t => t.amount).reduce(...), using the file's existing num helper) and narrow the parent's deletion from the child count alone to the amounts: when at most one child would remain (the existing deleteParentTransaction condition) AND that total does not equal the parent's amount, return { updated: [ makeTransactionWithChildCategory(parentTransaction, newNonChildTransactions[0]) with `error: null` ], deleted: childTransactions }. When the children do sum to the parent, fall through to the existing path unchanged. Add a comment naming the invariant: a parent may only be deleted when the children account for it. Return the parent THROUGH makeTransactionWithChildCategory — do not merely flip the deleteParentTransaction boolean, which leaves the row is_parent: true and is worse than today.
files.why: Fix for finding 2. Deletion is decided by remainingChildTransactions.length <= 1 alone, so a register-made split (two 0.00 children) makes the count say 'safe' while the amounts say the parent holds the only value and the occurrence stamp. The single-child branch at :452 already implements the correct behaviour; this generalises it to N children. `error: null` clears a stale SplitTransactionError the spread would otherwise carry onto a row that is no longer part of a split.

files.change: Comment only. The block at :586-597 explains that splits:'all' is required for the post guard and names getHasTransactionsQuery and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery as consumers that already pass it. Extend it to name the forecast as the fourth reader, now corrected.
files.why: No behaviour change — the guard itself is correct and was fixed by #69. A stale list of the correct readers is how the forecast reading drifted in the first place.

cases: does not re-project a posted occurrence whose transaction has been split — post a weekly schedule occurrence through the real handlers, split the posted row and give the two children half the amount each, assert the occurrence's data point has an empty `transactions` array and the running balance counts the real rows once. Today the point carries a projected entry of the full amount and the balance is 10000 too low from that date on.
keeps projecting the next occurrence after a split — control arm pinning that the fix removes the duplicate rather than all projection for a split-posted schedule.

unsplitting a split whose children were never filled in keeps the parent and its amount — 12345 stamped parent with two 0.00 children, unsplit both: one updated row at 12345 with `is_parent: false`, both children deleted, nothing at 0. The reproduced QA defect. Assert `is_parent: false` explicitly: narrowing only the deleteParentTransaction boolean leaves the row a split parent.

unsplitting that same parent leaves the occurrence stamp on the surviving row — the returned row still carries schedule and schedule_occurrence, which is what keeps /schedules reading Paid instead of Due. Asserted directly rather than inferred from the amount.
the surviving row carries no stale SplitTransactionError — the promoted row's `error` is null, so the row is not rendered with a split error against an amount that is present.

unsplitting a FILLED split still splits it out — 12345 parent with children 5000 and 7345, unsplit both: two updated children at their own amounts and the parent deleted. Guards against the fix over-reaching into correctly-filled splits.

unsplitting one child of a filled split still leaves the parent — 12345 parent with children 4000/4000/4345, unsplit the first: the parent survives at 8345 with the promoted child alongside and nothing deleted.

unsplitting two of three partially-typed children keeps the parent at its full amount — 12345 parent with children 5000/4000/0, unsplit the first two: the parent survives at 12345. This is the shape where the parent's amount and the typed partial amounts genuinely disagree, and it pins the rule this fix adopts so the choice is visible rather than incidental.

the existing case 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split' continues to pass and remains the one that fails when the guard's splits:'all' is reverted — the rename in finding 3 must not move that coverage onto the renamed case. I ran this: reverting the guard gives exactly `1 failed | 51 passed`, the failure being that sibling.

acceptance.check: A schedule occurrence whose posted transaction has been split into children is not counted a second time as a future payment in the balance forecast: the occurrence's day shows no projected transaction, and the running balance from that date counts the real rows once.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Demo budget: create a weekly schedule for a fixed amount (-100 on Checking), let one occurrence post, split the posted register row and give the two children amounts summing to the original (-50, -50). Open the balance forecast (Reports > Overview, the Balance Forecast card) over a window covering it. Before the fix the day carries a projected -100 on top of the real -100 and the balance is 100 too low; after, no projected entry and the balance reflects only the real rows. The next occurrence is still projected.

acceptance.check: Both stamp readers pass splits:'all', so the guard and the forecast's occurrence-posted check agree and neither is blind to a split parent. Pinned by execution, not by the type: TransactionEntity is structurally assignable to PostedScheduleTransaction, so the retyped parameter does not by itself prevent the inline set being passed back.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Revert `.options({ splits: 'all' })` from the guard at schedules/app.ts and run the schedules suite: 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split' must fail. Separately, revert the forecast's use of getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery back to `transactions` and run the forecast suite: the new split-occurrence case must fail. Both directions pinned. The retyped parameter alone produces no compile error on the revert, so the suite failure is the gate.

acceptance.check: Unsplitting a posted schedule payment that was split but never filled in leaves the payment standing alone at its original amount, with no stale split error on it, and the occurrence stays marked paid.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Demo budget: add a one-off schedule (amount 123.45, date a few days out) and post it from the row's actions menu ('Post transaction', not '…today'). In the register select the posted row, click its Category cell, choose Split, leave both new rows at 0.00. Right-click the split, choose 'Unsplit 1 transactions'. The 123.45 row must remain standing alone with its schedule badge and no split error; the 0.00 rows are gone. /schedules still reads Paid and its preview row is gone.

acceptance.check: Unsplitting a correctly filled split still produces the separate transactions, and the surviving row of a partially-typed one is not left as a split parent — the fix does not collapse or malform splits the user did fill in.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Split a 123.45 register row, enter 50.00 and 73.45 into the two children, 'Unsplit 1 transactions'. Two rows of 50.00 and 73.45 and no parent. Covered by unit tests in both directions (children summing to the parent; only some children unsplit); the browser check confirms the same shape behaves as before.

acceptance.check: The test case reporting a split-parented occurrence as posted is named for what it asserts, and the guard it used to claim to pin is pinned by the sibling case instead.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Read the case in packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.test.ts: name and comment must not claim agreement with the guard and must point at 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split'. Reverting the guard's splits:'all' must fail only that sibling — verified: 1 failed | 51 passed, the failure being the sibling.

acceptance.check: readSplitFamily reads the split family through AQL, in the same idiom as every other assertion in the file, with no internal-view reference and no integer-date detour — and its assertions use AQL's value conventions, so the suite still passes.
acceptance.how_to_verify: The helper issues a q('transactions') query with `.options({ splits: 'all' })` and an $or over id/parent_id; neither it nor the assertion below mentions v_transactions_internal or a 20170102 integer; the child assertions use toBeFalsy() and the parent assertion expects is_parent: true, because AQL returns booleans and undefined where the raw view returned 1 and null. Suite passes — verified at 52/52 with these exact edits; without the convention changes it fails on 'expected undefined to be null'.

qa_script: Boot the demo budget via 'View demo' on the initial setup screen (after 'Don't use a server') — an empty budget has no schedules to exercise the schedule cases.

AC-3 first, since it is the one with visible data loss: add a one-off schedule (payee QA Unsplit Then Post, account Bank of America, amount 123.45, date a few days out). Post it from the row's actions menu ('Post transaction', not '…today'). In the register select the posted row, click its Category cell, choose Split, leave both new rows at 0.00. Right-click the split and choose 'Unsplit 1 transactions'. Expect the 123.45 row to remain standing alone with its schedule badge and no split error, and the two 0.00 rows gone. Check /schedules: the occurrence must still read Paid and its preview row must be gone. Before the fix the 123.45 row disappears entirely, only the 0.00 rows remain, and /schedules reads Due with the preview row back.

AC-4 immediately after, on a split before it is unsplit: enter 50.00 and 73.45 into the two children, then 'Unsplit 1 transactions'. Expect two separate rows of 50.00 and 73.45 and no 123.45 parent — a filled split must still split out. On the unsplit row, also confirm it behaves as an ordinary transaction (no split affordance, no 'Unassigned amount' error) rather than as a leftover split parent.

AC-1: add a weekly schedule on Checking for -100. Let one occurrence post, then split the posted register row and give the two children -50.00 each. Open the balance forecast (Reports > Overview) over a window covering that occurrence and the next. Expect NO projected entry on the occurrence's day and the balance counting the real rows once; the following week's occurrence must still be projected. Before the fix a projected -100 sits on top of the real -100 and the balance is 100 too low.

The partially-typed case, which is the one to watch and is not in the ticket's repro: split a 123.45 row, type 50.00 into ONE child and leave the other empty, then unsplit both. Expect one row at 123.45 and the typed 50.00 gone. That is the rule this fix adopts and it is a visible change; confirm it, and report it in the PR description rather than letting a reviewer find it.

At PR time, not in the browser: confirm the PR title begins with '[AI] ' per .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md (#69's did not, nor did 71, 68, 67 or 65), and that both upcoming-release-notes/fix-unsplit-empty-split.md and the edited fix-split-occurrence-double-post.md appear in files[] along with every other changed path.
risks: The partially-typed split semantics are a product judgement, not a derivation from the code. A parent with children 5000/4000/0 is kept at its full 12345 and the typed 9000 is discarded; today the parent is reduced to the typed amounts and 2345 is lost instead. Both sides lose money on that shape. If a maintainer decides the typed partials should win, the condition narrows to a children-sum-of-zero test and nothing else in the order moves. Pinned by a test, in qa_script, and named here as the one place a maintainer may overrule.

The guard fires on child count as well as amount, so unsplitting a subset of children from a never-filled split deletes the children the user did not select too. The money outcome is right (the parent survives at its full amount, verified on the three-child shapes) but it dissolves the whole split. Worth a reviewer confirming that reads as intentional.

Clearing the promoted parent's `error` is a scope judgement, not something the ticket asked for. The consequence of not doing it is a stale SplitTransactionError object on the returned row. Note the reachability is narrower than an earlier draft of the plan claimed: the desktop register's `hasSplitError` in TransactionsTable.tsx:2767 gates on `trans.is_parent || trans.is_child`, and the promoted row has `is_parent: false` with no `is_child`, so the desktop badge would NOT render. The mobile editor (TransactionEdit.tsx:306) checks only `transaction.error?.type === 'SplitTransactionError'` with no such gate, so it WOULD show a split action against a row with a correct amount. Clearing it is still right — the value is a persisted json column (server/aql/schema/index.ts:47), so the stale object survives the round-trip — but the visible symptom is mobile-only.

The added AQL query on the forecast's hot path is unmeasured. Correctness was verified; latency was not, and there is no benchmark in the repo for this handler. It mirrors what useSchedules already runs.

The retype in forecast-schedules.ts is documentation, not a guard — TransactionEntity is structurally assignable to PostedScheduleTransaction, so the inline set could be passed back and would still compile. The tests are what hold the fix; do not let a reviewer read the narrow type as enforcement.
The release-note split is a judgement call a maintainer may reverse by merging the two note bodies.

This order changes no file under .sdlc/**, .github/**, docs/spec/**, docs/prd.md, docs/trd.md or docs/ui.md. The one place the plan would have liked to is .github/** — wiring release-notes-check.mjs into a workflow so release-note front matter became a machine-checked gate — and it is left out deliberately; see out_of_scope.
out_of_scope: Retitling PR #69 to carry the [AI] prefix — a one-word change to a merged PR's title, not a code change, so it cannot appear in files[], and editing another PR's title is outward-facing. Recorded in qa_script for this PR's own title and in residual_risks; deliberately not an AC, per the brief's prior rejection.

Wiring release-notes-check.mjs into a CI workflow so release-note front matter becomes a machine-checked gate. That is a change to .github/**, which no ticket here may touch, and is repo policy rather than a fix for #72.
Making the schedule stamp survive an unsplit by re-stamping the promoted children — a design question about what the stamp means, not a follow-up to this defect.
E2E coverage for the unsplit path; there is no Playwright test for the register's 'Unsplit' action today. Unit cases plus browser checks cover the reported defect.
The other consumers of getTransactions — they are balance uses and want the children.
Whether the forecast should itemise a split-parented occurrence's children as separate projected rows rather than suppressing the projection.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: I re-derived all six findings rather than accepting the proposal, and verified the four testable ones by execution on this tree: the unsplit defect by calling the function directly and reproducing the data loss; finding 3 by reverting the guard and watching the right sibling fail; finding 4 by applying the AQL rewrite and getting 52/52; finding 1 by reading the full data path from getTransactions' splits:'inline' through executors.ts's `is_parent = 0` filter to indexPostedScheduleTransactions. I then applied both fixes and measured them — six row shapes for the unsplit, the forecast suite plus a full 1268-test loot-core run plus a six-workspace typecheck with both applied — and reverted everything, so the tree is clean. What holds this below the high 80s is the partially-typed split: I measured both sides of the change and each loses money on that shape, so the rule is a defensible product judgement rather than a derivation, and a maintainer may reasonably overrule it. Also deducted: I found one load-bearing error in the proposal's evidence — the stale-split-error claim cites a desktop code path that is gated on is_parent/is_child and would not render, so the real symptom is mobile-only (the fix is still right, the reason was wrong); and the fifth query on the forecast's hot path is unmeasured for latency. None of these change what the code does. What would move the number up: a maintainer ruling on the partially-typed shape, and a latency measurement on the added query. Down: if the desktop badge really is the intended symptom of the error change, or if the mobile path turns out to re-derive the error from the children on the next read, the error fix would need re-scoping.

The array is used for the posted-check only — it does not reach projectForecastData.

Arbiter verification, finding 2. Called makeAsNonChildTransactions directly on a 12345 stamped parent with two 0.00 children: updated=[{amount:0},{amount:0}], deleted=[{amount:12345,schedule:'s1'}]. The payment and its stamp are gone.

Arbiter verification, fix B, six shapes. Applied the narrow-and-return-parent fix: unfilled 2-child unsplit-all returns the 12345 stamped parent with is_parent:false and both children deleted; FILLED 5000/7345 still splits out; partial 5000/0 keeps the parent at 12345; filled 3-child unselecting one leaves the parent at 8345 with the promoted child; 3-child unselecting two keeps the parent at 12345; zero-amount parent with zero children unchanged. Also measured the cheaper variant the order rejects: narrowing only the deleteParentTransaction boolean leaves is_parent:true on the surviving row.
Arbiter verification, full suite. Both fixes applied: loot-core 87 files, 1268 passed, 1 expected fail, 2 skipped, exit 0. Tree restored clean afterwards; only plan/ is untracked.

Arbiter verification, finding 3. Removed `.options({ splits: 'all' })` from the guard in schedules/app.ts and ran src/server/schedules/app.test.ts: 'Tests 1 failed | 51 passed (52)', the failure being 'writes no second transaction when the posted one has been split'. 'leaves the status queries agreeing with the guard after a split' passed with the guard removed. Restored.

Arbiter verification, finding 4, and a correction to the proposal. Applied the AQL rewrite of readSplitFamily plus the rename: 52/52 passed. The convention changes are load-bearing — without `is_parent: true` instead of `is_parent: 1` and `toBeFalsy()` instead of `toBeNull()` the rewrite fails on 'expected undefined to be null'. The select list must include 'schedule'; the proposal's earlier draft omitted it.

Arbiter correction to the proposal's stale-error evidence. The proposal cited TransactionsTable.tsx:2766 as computing hasSplitError 'without checking the row is still half of a live split'. It does check: line 2767 gates on `(trans.is_parent || trans.is_child)`, and the promoted row has is_parent:false with no is_child, so the desktop badge would not render. The mobile editor (TransactionEdit.tsx:306) checks only `transaction.error?.type === 'SplitTransactionError'` with no such gate, so the symptom is real there. `error` is a persisted json column (server/aql/schema/index.ts:47), so the stale value survives the round-trip. The fix (`error: null`) stands; the stated reason is corrected in risks and residual_risks.

alternatives_considered.approach: Change getTransactions in forecast-filters.ts to pass splits:'all' so the forecast can see the split parent.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the symptom by breaking the balance projection. That query's inline split set is load-bearing: projectForecastData sums the CHILDREN's amounts, because the parent is not additive with them. Widening it double-counts every split — the existing test 'does not double-count split parents in posted transaction balances' is exactly that guard. The two consumers need opposite split types, so they need separate queries.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add splits:'all' only for the schedule-occurrence columns, by selecting them off a second filtered query rather than reusing getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The query already exists, already passes splits:'all', and already returns exactly the ['schedule','date','schedule_occurrence'] shape the consumers are typed on. A variant means a second place that must remember the splits rule — which is how the forecast drifted in the first place.

alternatives_considered.approach: For the unsplit defect, narrow the existing `deleteParentTransaction` boolean alone, without returning the parent through makeTransactionWithChildCategory.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: I applied this first and measured it: it stops the amount loss but leaves the row with `is_parent: true` and a spread of the parent, so the user is left with a split parent carrying no children — a worse outcome than today's, and one the table still renders as part of a split. The helper is what sets is_parent: false and takes the category from the promoted child.

alternatives_considered.approach: For the unsplit defect, carry the parent's residual onto one of the promoted children instead of keeping the parent.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It must invent a rule for which child absorbs the difference, and produces two rows where the user had one transaction. The function already has the right answer one branch above — the single-child case keeps the parent at its own amount; generalising it invents nothing.

alternatives_considered.approach: For the unsplit defect, refuse the unsplit outright when the children do not sum to the parent, surfacing an error.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Unsplitting is a user-initiated revert of a split they made moments earlier, and the register already shows the split error on the row. Blocking moves the problem rather than fixing it and leaves the count-vs-amount decision in place.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 3, add `await post(id)` after the split in the 'status queries agreeing' case so it pins the guard, rather than renaming it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is a framing gap, not missing coverage: the sibling already pins the guard and fails when it is reverted, which I confirmed by running it (1 failed | 51 passed, the failure being the sibling). A second copy duplicates coverage in the same file for no new signal.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the unsplit defect in the desktop-client caller (Account.tsx onMakeAsNonSplitTransactions) rather than in makeAsNonChildTransactions.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That puts the invariant in the one UI that happens to call it today, at the wrong layer: the function is what decides a parent is safe to delete. The only production call sites are Account.tsx:1242 and :1266, both inside onMakeAsNonSplitTransactions, and the api package does not reach it — but the caller does not know the amounts and the function does.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fold the unsplit fix's release note into the existing schedule-occurrence note, as an earlier draft did, on the grounds that both fixes share a root cause and one symptom.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The root cause and symptom are shared between the forecast fix and the split-occurrence fix, not between those and the unsplit fix. Unsplitting a never-filled split destroys the amount of any register row, schedule or not, and the schedule is only how QA happened to hit it. One note titled for schedule occurrences would misdescribe a general register defect and hide it from users who never used a schedule.

alternatives_considered.approach: Split the ticket: one work order for the forecast finding, another for the unsplit finding, deferring the two test-file findings to a docs-only change.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The two defects are two views of the same interaction — what happens to a schedule payment once it has been split — and both end in the occurrence being miscounted. They are not separable by risk either: the unsplit fix is the wider-reaching and the forecast fix is a one-line argument change, so 'do the small one first' does not apply. Splitting would also mean two PRs racing on the same test files.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep AC-7 and AC-8 — the [AI] PR prefix and the release note's slug and front matter — as acceptance criteria, but re-verify them as `test` rather than `browser`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The brief's prior rejection was right that no live run can decide either. Marking them `test` only moves the problem: there is no CI case that checks a PR title, and release-notes-check.mjs is wired into no workflow today, so no run decides the note's front matter either. Wiring it up is a change to .github/**, which no ticket here may touch. They live in qa_script and out_of_scope instead, where a human reads them at PR time.

assumptions: The demo budget QA boots ('View demo' after 'Don't use a server') has accounts and enough data to exercise schedules; the project's own AGENTS.md recommends it for exactly this reason.
The register's Category-cell split and the right-click 'Unsplit N transactions' item are the two affordances QA drives for AC-3 and AC-4, per the QA repro in the issue.
unknowns: Whether the partially-typed split case (some children typed, sum short of the parent) has a settled product answer distinct from the never-filled one. This order adopts the rule keeping the parent's full amount, and both sides of that choice lose money.

Whether unsplitting a FILLED split whose children sum to the parent but whose parent carries an occurrence stamp is exercised anywhere in the e2e suite. No e2e coverage for the unsplit path was found at all, which is why AC-3 and AC-4 are verified in a browser as well.

Whether the forecast is the only remaining consumer reading the stamp off an inline split set. The guard, the two status queries and the forecast were enumerated by grep; a reader querying the stamp column directly could not be ruled out.
Whether a fifth query on the forecast's hot path is acceptable on a budget with many schedules. Correctness was verified, not latency, and there is no benchmark in the repo for this handler.
validated_work_order.debate_summary:
There was no debate: `plan/critique.json` is `{}` — the critic wrote nothing, so there were no findings to judge or dismiss, and the arbitration rests entirely on my own reading of the code and the issue. I say this plainly because a tidy 'the council agreed' summary would misrepresent what happened.

What I did instead of judging a critique was re-derive the proposal from scratch, and it largely survives: all six findings hold, and I independently reproduced the two code defects and the two test-file findings by execution rather than by reading the prior report's conclusions. Four things I checked myself rather than accept:

The forecast's diagnosis is right, and I confirmed the whole chain rather than the summary of it — the query is `.options({ splits: 'inline' })`, executors.ts appends `is_parent = 0` for every split type but 'all', the array reaches indexPostedScheduleTransactions and nothing else, and splitTransaction keeps the stamp on the parent while makeChild copies neither field. A correct reader already exists. Applying the fix passed the forecast suite and a six-workspace typecheck.

The unsplit fix's shape is right, and I rejected one thing the proposal did not: narrowing the `deleteParentTransaction` boolean ALONE. I implemented that cheaper version first and measured it — it stops the amount loss but leaves the surviving row `is_parent: true`, which is worse than today's bug. The fix has to route the parent through `makeTransactionWithChildCategory`, which is what sets `is_parent: false`. That requirement is now explicit in files[] because the obvious cheaper edit does not work.

The proposal's stale-split-error evidence is wrong, and this is the one place I corrected rather than confirmed. It cites TransactionsTable.tsx:2766 as computing `hasSplitError` without checking the row is still half of a live split. Line 2767 does check — it gates on `(trans.is_parent || trans.is_child)`, and the promoted row is `is_parent: false` with no `is_child`, so the desktop badge would not render. The symptom is real, but on mobile: TransactionEdit.tsx:306 tests only `transaction.error?.type === 'SplitTransactionError'` with no such gate. The `error: null` change itself stands — `error` is a persisted json column, so the stale object survives the round-trip — but the reason is corrected in risks, and the visible symptom is narrowed to mobile so a reviewer does not go looking for a desktop badge that will not appear.

I also verified the AQL rewrite of readSplitFamily end to end and confirmed the proposal's own correction of an earlier draft: the rewrite fails without the assertion-convention changes (`is_parent: true` not `1`, `toBeFalsy()` not `toBeNull()`), and passes 52/52 with them. I added that to files[] as required rather than optional, and to AC-6.

On the brief's one prior rejection — AC-7/AC-8 as browser criteria nothing in the product can decide — the proposal honoured it by dropping both from acceptance[], and I agree with where they went (qa_script and out_of_scope). I considered re-instating them as `test` and rejected that: there is no CI case for a PR title, and release-notes-check.mjs is wired into no workflow, so no run decides either one. Wiring it up would touch .github/**, which this ticket may not do.

What I did not do is split the ticket, agreeing with the proposal: the two defects are two views of one interaction, and the wider-reaching one is not the smaller one, so 'do the small one first' buys nothing. A maintainer who disagrees can lift the files[] entries out cleanly.

The honest weak spot, which I am not tidying: the partially-typed split rule is a judgement, and I measured that it loses money on both sides of the change. It is pinned by a test, in qa_script, and named as the one thing a maintainer may overrule — but it is a judgement, not a derivation.
residual_risks: The partially-typed split semantics are a product judgement and this is where the change is both visible and lossy — see risks. Measured both sides: with the fix 12345 survives and 9000 typed is discarded; today 9000 survives and 2345 is lost. The case is in qa_script so it is checked and reported rather than discovered by a reviewer.
The guard dissolves a whole split when the user unsplits only some children. The money outcome is right but the behaviour is visible; a reviewer should confirm it reads as intentional.

The stale-error fix targets a mobile-only symptom (see risks). If a reviewer reads the desktop badge as the reason, the justification is wrong even though clearing the field is right — the value is persisted and the mobile editor renders it ungated.
The added AQL query on the forecast's hot path is unmeasured for latency; a budget with many schedules may read more rows than the old path.

The [AI] prefix omission is systemic across pipeline-authored PRs 65, 67, 68, 69 and 71, and nothing in this order fixes the pipeline that produced the other four. It is a qa_script step rather than an acceptance criterion because no browser run and no existing CI case can decide it — the same reason release-note contents are not an AC. If the pipeline's PR-creation step is the real defect, that is a maintainer-stage change, not part of #72.
The caller sweep for makeAsNonChildTransactions covered packages/ excluding node_modules; a consumer reaching it through a generated or dynamic import path would not have appeared.

The three-child register affordance — the Category-cell split versus the right-click 'Unsplit N transactions' item — is exercised only by unit tests; QA's repro and the browser checks use two children.
